lines.text: Once, a footballer knelt down and begged his country to stop a war. And it listened.
No trophy he ever won meant more. And tonight, the Peacemaker's spirit is watching.
Last time, we predicted the Netherlands would edge Sweden, two to one.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode thirty-six. Germany... versus the Ivory Coast.
The four-time champions against the Elephants. And stay with me — because one of these nations once used football to stop the fighting.
Two nations bound by more than a game. Tonight, they collide.
First, the history. Germany. Four World Cups. A machine built to win.
Champions in fifty-four, seventy-four, ninety, and two thousand fourteen — nobody does ruthless quite like them.
Musiala and Wirtz are the new golden generation. Born three months apart, they seem to read each other's minds.
When Germany click, they are almost impossible to stop.
But tonight, they face a nation with a story football has never forgotten.
The Ivory Coast. In two thousand five, this team qualified for their first World Cup as a civil war tore their country apart.
And in the dressing room, Didier Drogba fell to his knees and begged for peace. Within days, the guns fell silent.
A golden generation — Drogba, Yaya Toure, Gervinho — dazzled the world, yet never escaped the group.
This is a new Ivory Coast. Younger. Hungrier. Determined to finish what the legends started.
The machine against the Elephants. Tonight, something has to give.
Now, Germany. Jamal Musiala — they call him Bambi, and he dances through defences like they are not there.
Florian Wirtz threads the impossible. Kai Havertz leads the line. Joshua Kimmich and Antonio Rudiger hold the spine.
German precision — cold, clinical, relentless.
And across from them — the Ivory Coast. Amad Diallo, whose dribbling turns defenders into traffic cones.
Franck Kessie powers the midfield. Simon Adingra brings the pace. Ousmane Diomande anchors the back.
So here is the duel. German machinery... against the speed and soul of the Elephants.
Our prediction — built on German quality, and on an Ivory Coast side with nothing to fear. Watch.
The twenty-fourth minute. Wirtz finds him, and Jamal Musiala dances in to finish. One-nil, Germany.
But the Elephants answer. Kessie drives, Adingra crosses, and Amad Diallo volleys it home. One-all.
The stadium loses its mind. Ter Stegen keeps Germany alive with a fingertip save.
Then German quality tells. Kai Havertz rises to head the winner. Two-one, Germany.
Two-one at the whistle, in our story. The machine edges it — but the Elephants made them tremble.
Do you agree? Comment GERMANY if the machine wins. Comment ELEPHANTS if the Ivory Coast shock them.
And that spirit in the stands? Legend number thirty-six: the Peacemaker.
The man who proved a game can be bigger than a war. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to you. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score, scores for you.
Free to play, no prizes. Like, share, subscribe — the legends are only beginning.
